questions.question: For a discrete distribution, what does a mode maximize?
options: The cumulative distribution function at every point
The probability mass function
The variance
The sample size

questions.question: For a continuous distribution, what does a mode maximize?
options: The probability of a single exact value
The distribution's sample size
The probability density function
The event complement

questions.question: Can a distribution have more than one mode?
options: No, every distribution has exactly one mode
Only if it has no PMF or PDF
Only if probabilities are negative
Yes, it may have several modes

questions.question: Where is the mode of a normal distribution?
options: At both tails
At every real number
At the variance only
At its center

questions.question: If a PMF has probabilities $0.1,0.6,0.3$ at values $1,2,3$, what is the mode?
options: $0.6$ as a value of $X$

questions.question: A mixture of two separated normal distributions can have how many modes?
options: No possible modes
Exactly one mode always
Two modes
One mode at every point

questions.question: If two discrete values both have the largest probability, what are they?
options: Neither can be a mode
Only the smaller value is a mode
Both are modes
Only the larger value is a mode

questions.question: How is a mode different from a mean?
options: A mode is a most likely value; a mean is an average.
A mode is an average value; a mean is a most likely value.
A mode splits the probability in half; a mean is an average.
A mode is a most likely value; a mean is a middle value.

questions.question: Why can a fair die have every face as a mode?
options: The die has no probability mass function
The mode must equal the median
All faces tie for the maximum probability mass
Each of the faces has a probability greater than one

questions.question: Why should one be careful interpreting a continuous mode as 'most probable exact value'?
options: Continuous densities never have a single highest point.
Point probabilities are zero for continuous RVs.
The mode of a continuous RV always equals its mean.
The density at the mode is the probability of the mode.

questions.question: A distribution's mode is its most probable value. Which situation gives 'no unique mode'?
options: The mean and the median take different values
The mass function is strictly decreasing in $x$
The density has a single peak that is not symmetric
The maximum may be attained at more than one value

questions.question: Why is the mode a shape-related summary?
options: It measures how widely the values are spread.
It identifies peaks of the mass or density.
It is a weighted average of the possible values.
It identifies the endpoints of the support.

questions.question: A student says a fair die has mode $3.5$ because that is its center. What is wrong?
options: The mode is a value of maximum probability mass.
A fair die has no mode, since all faces tie.
The mode must be rounded to the nearest face, $4$.
Nothing; the mode of a symmetric law is its centre.

questions.question: If a continuous density is constant on $[0,1]$, what happens to the mode?
options: Only the midpoint $1/2$ is a mode, by symmetry.
All points of $[0,1]$ attain the max density.
There is no mode, since no peak stands out.
Only the endpoints $0$ and $1$ are modes.
